claims.statement: Planar slicing preprocesses mesh cross-sections into layers and islands, computes dirty steps in worker threads, then globally orders, modifies, reorients, and writes the resulting paths.

The Preprocessor sorts build, clipping, and settings parts, copies global settings plus part overrides, copies each build mesh, and exposes ordered callbacks from initial processing through final processing.

Planar preprocessing rejects overlapping settings masks inside build cross-sections, clears prior build steps, clips copied meshes with target-scoped clippers, adds layer structures and populates global layers.

A planar SliceMeta snapshot contains effective settings, cross-section geometry, slicing plane, settings polygons, average normal, and flattening shifts; disconnected polygon parts become separate PolymerIsland objects.
Successive planar slicing planes move by half the previous layer height plus half the current layer height, placing the plane at the center of each layer band even when layer heights vary.

The ordinary cross-section path intersects non-ignored triangles, flattens segments into XY, reconnects and stitches open polylines, optionally smooths them, removes degenerate vertices, and simplifies closed polygons.

Effective layer settings apply global adjustments, part overrides, matching settings-range overrides, and layer-index local adjustments before settings-part masks are separately attached as SettingsPolygon objects.
SettingsPolygon masks are interpreted by individual regions: infill partitions fill geometry for local spacing and angle, while perimeter contours are split into subsegments carrying local settings.

Variable layer height is currently restricted to enabled JuggerBot slicing and clamps a cusp-error-derived height between configured minimum and standard heights; computeSliceCount repeats the production height and plane decisions.
Polymer islands instantiate enabled perimeter, inset, skin, infill, and skeleton regions in configured order, and island computation passes remaining polygon geometry from each region to the next.

TraditionalAST queues every dirty non-clipping step, computes steps independently with up to the ideal thread count, and begins postprocessing only after all queued work completes or immediately when nothing is dirty.
LayerOrderOptimizer builds global layers by height with tolerance, by layer number, or by part.
A global layer uses common layer-local island-order settings when compatible, but conflicting methods or incompatible projected custom anchors fall back to global settings.

Within a global layer, scans are connected first, skirts precede main print islands, rafts exclude ordinary build/support ordering, support-first controls support versus polymer precedence, and brims impose containment order.

Planar region optimization chooses path and point order in the flattened slicing frame, can use the prior layer's printing start for continuity, applies path modifiers, prepends travel, and updates the shared current location.
Connected contour grouping joins eligible nested loops within a width-based connector limit and splits unrelated or non-adjacent loops into separate groups that require travel.
Planar postprocessing un-orients paths, connects and orders them, applies global modifiers and eligible arc fitting, and then reorients paths to printer coordinates.
Planar arc fitting requires G3 support, a writer syntax that emits arcs, planar mode, and an exact positive-Z slicing normal.
Forward-tip-wipe connections rotate seams, seek angled branches, validate emitted loop and branch eligibility, and flush unsafe groups into separate paths.

Perimeter-to-inset connections require adjacent region order, enabled chain controls, inset geometry and compatible effective materials for this island; only consumed inset output is cleared and localized inset segment settings are preserved.
Planar settings overlaps are tested in actual sliced build geometry and fail preprocessing explicitly before worker dispatch.
Planar child settings/clipping scope includes enabled direct children of the target build part alongside enabled root modifiers.
Support contact restoration grows angle-classified contacts inside convex cells of each unsupported component and clips growth to those cells and components, preventing gap-crossing restoration.
Bridge suppression requires complete opposing exterior anchor bands within the length limit, considering polygon-edge directions and a two-micron tolerance for rotated spans.
Organic support retains original angle-classified seeds, combines forced contact, clips to surviving demand and falls back inside a restored component only when it has no surviving seed.
